A Vprog is an app that runs on its own node, keeps its own state and posts zero knowledge proof of that state back to Casper. Now Casper already has smart contracts, covenants, live on mainnet since June, straight from the core devs. Vprogs are the next layer up, whole applications on a chain that already runs 10 blocks every single second. So let's break this all down. So back in 2020 Vitalik laid out Ethereum's plan and it said in plain English, all in on rollups, your accounts, your businesses, your assets living inside a layer 2. And every rollup is its own chain, its own sequencer, the machine that orders your transactions, its own bridge, its own slice of liquidity. And every one of those pieces is a place for something to break and a place for your liquidity to get split up. Now Casper's founder, Janitem Sampalinski looked at all of that and back in December he said the whole point of Vprogs was to avoid the obsolete path of L2s. His words, not mine. And he hasn't softened on it. So here's how a Vprog actually works. You send a transaction and you declare upfront which account it reads and which one it writes. Casper does 4 jobs. It orders every transaction, so Casper itself is the sequencer. It stores the data, it checks the proofs, it meters the work. What it never does is run the app. The app runs on its own nodes. Every Vprog owns its own accounts and it's the only thing allowed to write to them. And Provers, for-profit operators, post a zero-knowledge proof back to Casper.
